about: A second subject for the evaluation, so the numbers do not depend on one document. Each question has an answer_contains phrase copied from sample_notes_physics.txt. A retrieval counts as a hit when one of the returned chunks contains that phrase. kind: 'paraphrase' = the question shares few words with the answer, 'exact' = it asks about a specific name, number, term or formula, 'synonym' = the question uses different words for the same thing.
unanswerable: What is the speed of light in a vacuum?
How does a nuclear reactor produce electricity?
What is the boiling point of water in kelvin?
What is the capital of Japan?

questions.q: Why does a person standing in a bus fall forwards when it stops quickly?
questions.answer_contains: A passenger in a bus lurches forward when the driver brakes suddenly

questions.answer_contains: One newton is the force that gives a mass of one kilogram

questions.q: What does Newton's second law say?
questions.answer_contains: directly proportional to the net force on it and inversely proportional to its mass

questions.q: What acceleration does a 20 N force give a 4 kg trolley?
questions.answer_contains: A force of 20 N acting on a trolley of mass 4 kg gives an acceleration of 5 m/s2

questions.q: Why can the action and reaction forces of the third law not cancel out?
questions.answer_contains: The two forces act on different objects, so they never cancel each other

questions.q: What is the formula for gravitational potential energy?
questions.answer_contains: PE = mgh

questions.answer_contains: energy can never be created or destroyed

questions.q: How many watts are in a kilowatt?

questions.answer_contains: This is why the lamps in a house are wired in parallel

questions.q: How far away must a surface be for an echo to be heard clearly?
questions.answer_contains: heard clearly only if the reflecting surface is at least 17 m away
